THE LADDER: Why 1 asks who pays, and why the price moved. Each Why is answered from evidence on two domains, a filing, a contract, a pricing page, a royalty split, or it is marked as an open question and the ladder stops there; a Why is never climbed past without its evidence. Each rung joins the last with "because" or "but", never "and then", and ends on the next question. Three to seven rungs, five as the target, never padded. The channel covers the whole money system, from any side of the invoice: what a business can charge for AI-powered work, what AI actually costs to run and whether it pays back, how the labs themselves make money, and when it is worth owning the thing rather than renting it. A piece that traces one chain end to end is the best version of this channel. THE READER is anyone standing at the invoice, on either side of it: the leader of a five to fifty million pound business who has just seen the renewal quote, the operator setting a price for work a model now does, and the founder deciding whether to build the thing or keep renting it. SUBJECTS are giants, and after that whoever leaves the best paper trail. Product surfaces are evidence for the money question and are never a follow.the.money subject in their own right. THE BOUNDARY, and it decides every contested subject: what does the reader change next? If they would go and change a price, a budget or a contract, it is follow.the.money. If they would change what they build or buy, it is under.the.hood. If they would change how they think or what they expect, it is mind.the.gap. The question decides, never the surface. NAMING: name whoever the number came from. A public decision by a named executive is fair game; their character is not. THE LANDING: what the ladder shows about who ends up better or worse off, and the strongest version names something already fixed that has not yet shown up in the price (a lease, a depreciation schedule, a liability cap), then hands the reader one open question. Never a forecast, a date to check, odds or a confidence number. Diagram language: the money map, where the dollars enter and where they leave, one rung at a time. HARD GATES, applied before scoring. NOT US: the subject is never Krish, mind/make, CTRL or his own accounts, however available the material. MATERIAL EXISTS: if the evidence has to be created rather than found, it is not commissioned, however good the idea. THE BEAT: who gets paid when AI helps make creative work, in music, film and TV, games, art and design, theatre, media and creator tech: the money behind the hit, the royalty, the licence and the tool. Not governance, regulation, security or data breaches.

creators.why_it_works: It takes the obvious observation that agents got better and redirects the entire argument to organizational design, which is a more durable and less covered claim than another capability update.
creators.krish_angle: Krish's agentic operating system did not get faster when the models did, because the approval stack he inherited from a human-run business was still five layers deep; the actual unlock came from deleting three of those layers and publishing what broke when he did it.

creators.why_it_works: It reframes a resourcing question as a structural one, then earns it with specific before/after ratios from one real org rather than an industry survey, which makes the claim feel inspected rather than asserted.
creators.krish_angle: The handoff is the unit that breaks, not the headcount, and Krish's own agent fleet proves it differently: his bottleneck is not model output but how many of his own review gates a single human can staff before judgment becomes the rate limiter, with the actual gate-to-output ratio from his build published.

creators.why_it_works: the numbered list of specific, sometimes contradictory lessons reads as field notes rather than a pitch, which earns trust that a polished case study would not

Make a song in one app, post it in another, in one tap. Three months free. A song flying from one phone app straight onto a SoundCloud page. Thirty seconds of film from 15 of your own pictures. Fifteen photos on a corkboard becoming one moving shot. Kling 4.0 makes single AI video clips up to 30 seconds long from up to 15 of your own reference images or clips. For a small team, that is a storyboard you can watch.

house_rules.name: The big picture, never the small headline
house_rules.text: Every piece is about the big, lasting shift, never one small, temporary news headline. A headline of the week (a report, a price change, a launch) is evidence inside the bigger story, one section at most, and never the story itself. Before choosing an angle or a title, name the bigger pattern it belongs to and lead with that; if a draft would be out of date in a month, it is about the headline and must be reframed.

house_rules.name: One story, start to finish
house_rules.text: Every piece and every script tells one story. Open on one clear question, in plain words. Every section or beat either sets that question up or answers it, and each one follows from the last. Set up every claim before judging it: say what was claimed and why it matters before stamping it real or theatre. Every takeaway follows from something already told. The ending answers the opening question, then lands: what this shows, and an open question handed to the viewer. A spoken script of a minute or more then closes as SCRIPT_CLOSE says, after the landing: the one thing Krish would do, then where the full story is free to read; it never ends on the number.
